title: 137. Quantitative Relationships & Measurement: Harmonic Mean for Equal-Distance Speeds
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Harmonic Mean for Two Equal-Distance Speeds
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the average speed for a round trip over equal distances at two different speeds.
questions.question: A car travels from town A to town B at \(40\text{ km/h}\) and returns along the same road at \(60\text{ km/h}\). What is the average speed for the whole trip?
questions.explanation: For equal distances, the average speed is the harmonic mean of the two speeds: \(\frac{2v_1v_2}{v_1+v_2}\). Here, \(\frac{2\times 40\times 60}{40+60}=\frac{4{,}800}{100}=48\text{ km/h}\). The arithmetic mean \(50\text{ km/h}\) would be correct only if equal times were spent at each speed, not equal distances.
questions.hint: Start from total distance divided by total time.

questions.concept: Harmonic Mean of Two Speeds over Equal Distances
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the average speed over two equal-length segments at different speeds.
questions.question: A cyclist covers the first half of a journey at \(20\text{ km/h}\) and the second half at \(30\text{ km/h}\). What is the average speed for the entire journey?
questions.explanation: Because the two halves are equal in distance, the average speed is the harmonic mean: \(\frac{2\times 20\times 30}{20+30}=\frac{1{,}200}{50}=24\text{ km/h}\). The value \(25\text{ km/h}\) is the arithmetic mean, which does not apply here because equal distances, not equal times, are involved.
questions.hint: Equal distances do not generally take equal times.

questions.concept: Harmonic Mean of Three Equal-Distance Speeds
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the average speed over three equal-length segments at different speeds.
questions.question: A train travels three equal-length sections at \(20\text{ km/h}\), \(30\text{ km/h}\), and \(60\text{ km/h}\). What is the average speed for the whole journey? Round to two decimal places.
questions.hint: Express each travel time in terms of the common section length.

questions.concept: Finding a Missing Speed Using the Harmonic Mean
questions.learningObjective: Determine the return speed when the average speed and the outward speed are known.
questions.question: A car travels from P to Q at \(30\text{ km/h}\) and returns along the same road at a different speed. The average speed for the round trip is \(36\text{ km/h}\). What was the return speed?
questions.explanation: Let each leg have distance \(d\) and let the return speed be \(v\). Then \(\frac{2d}{\frac{d}{30}+\frac{d}{v}}=36\), giving \(\frac{1}{v}=\frac{2}{36}-\frac{1}{30}=\frac{1}{45}\). Thus \(v=45\text{ km/h}\). The alternative \(42\text{ km/h}\) solves \(\frac{30+v}{2}=36\), using an arithmetic mean for equal distances.
questions.hint: Start from total distance divided by total time.

questions.learningObjective: Compare the harmonic mean and arithmetic mean for two positive speeds.
questions.question: For the distinct positive speeds \(25\text{ km/h}\) and \(75\text{ km/h}\) over equal distances, which statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The harmonic mean is smaller than the arithmetic mean.

options.label: B
options.text: The harmonic mean is larger than the arithmetic mean.

questions.explanation: The harmonic mean is \(\frac{2}{\frac{1}{25}+\frac{1}{75}}=37.5\text{ km/h}\), whereas the arithmetic mean is \(\frac{25+75}{2}=50\text{ km/h}\). Thus the harmonic mean is smaller. The opposite inequality is incorrect for these distinct positive speeds.
questions.hint: Equal distances do not generally take equal times.

questions.concept: Harmonic Mean for a Round Trip
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the average speed for a round trip at two different speeds.
questions.question: A vehicle completes a round trip along the same road, going out at \(40\text{ km/h}\) and returning at \(120\text{ km/h}\). What is the average speed for the round trip?
questions.explanation: For equal distances, the average speed is \(\frac{2}{\frac{1}{40}+\frac{1}{120}}=60\text{ km/h}\). The alternative \(80\text{ km/h}\) is the arithmetic mean, which would apply to equal time intervals rather than equal distances.
questions.hint: Express each travel time in terms of the common section length.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the harmonic mean of two positive numbers.
questions.question: What is the harmonic mean of \(3\) and \(6\)?
questions.explanation: The harmonic mean of two numbers is \(\frac{2ab}{a+b}\). Here, \(\frac{2\times 3\times 6}{3+6}=\frac{36}{9}=4\). Therefore, the harmonic mean is \(4\). Option B is the arithmetic mean.
questions.hint: Average the reciprocals of the two numbers, then take the reciprocal of that average.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the average speed over two equal-length sections.
questions.question: A car travels the first half of a trip at \(60\text{ km/h}\) and the second half at \(90\text{ km/h}\). What is the average speed for the whole trip?
questions.explanation: For equal distances, the average speed is \(\frac{2}{\frac{1}{60}+\frac{1}{90}}=72\text{ km/h}\). The alternative \(75\text{ km/h}\) is the arithmetic mean and assumes equal travel times.
questions.hint: Equal distances do not generally take equal times.

questions.concept: Harmonic Mean of Three Equal-Distance Speeds
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the average speed over three equal-length segments at different speeds.
questions.question: A cyclist rides three equal-length sections at \(6\text{ km/h}\), \(12\text{ km/h}\), and \(4\text{ km/h}\). What is the average speed for the whole journey? Round to two decimal places.
questions.hint: Express each travel time in terms of the common section length.

questions.concept: Harmonic Mean for Three Equal-Distance Speeds
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the average speed over three equal-length segments at different speeds.
questions.question: A person travels three equal-length segments at \(30\text{ km/h}\), \(40\text{ km/h}\), and \(60\text{ km/h}\). What is the average speed for the entire journey? Round to two decimal places.
questions.hint: Start from total distance divided by total time.
